values.en: Unit Vector Orthogonal to Its Derivative
values.zh-CN: 单位向量与其导数正交

values.en: If a differentiable vector-valued function has constant norm $1$, that is $\lVert\gamma(t)\rVert\equiv 1$, then its derivative is orthogonal to it: $\gamma'(t)\perp\gamma(t)$, i.e. $\langle\gamma'(t),\gamma(t)\rangle=0$. Indeed $\lVert\gamma\rVert^{2}=\langle\gamma,\gamma\rangle$ is constant, so differentiating gives $2\langle\gamma',\gamma\rangle=0$. The converse fails in general: $\gamma'(t)\perp\gamma(t)$ need not force $\lVert\gamma\rVert$ to be constant, as $\gamma(t)=(t,1)$ shows. This is the fact used repeatedly in the sequel: each of $\mathbf{t},\mathbf{n},\mathbf{b}$ is a unit vector field, so each of their derivatives lies in the plane orthogonal to it.
values.zh-CN: 若可微的向量值函数具有常值范数 $1$，即 $\lVert\gamma(t)\rVert\equiv 1$，则其导数与其正交：$\gamma'(t)\perp\gamma(t)$，即 $\langle\gamma'(t),\gamma(t)\rangle=0$。事实上 $\lVert\gamma\rVert^{2}=\langle\gamma,\gamma\rangle$ 为常数，求导得 $2\langle\gamma',\gamma\rangle=0$。逆命题一般地不成立：由 $\gamma'(t)\perp\gamma(t)$ 未必推出 $\lVert\gamma\rVert$ 为常数，例如 $\gamma(t)=(t,1)$。这正是后文反复用到的事实：$\mathbf{t},\mathbf{n},\mathbf{b}$ 均为单位向量场，故它们各自的导数都落在与其正交的平面内。
